title: The deploy success signal never touches the worker, and /health has no worker or queue component
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:342-380 (both smoke phases are `docker compose exec -T app ...`); .github/workflows/deploy.yml:302 (`up -d --remove-orphans`, no --wait); scripts/llm_harness.py:94-145 (flow_core hard-asserts only /health, /creators/me, /videos + envelope shape); main.py:553-567 (/health = postgres+redis+storage only); docker-compose.prod.yml:49-53 and :75-80 (celery inspect ping healthchecks that nothing reads)
claims_to_verify: That the deployed release works: the deploy job's Phase-1 /health gate and Phase-2 `llm_harness.py --flow core` "critical journey" smoke, plus the one continuous production monitor (a Cloudflare Health Check on /health), together assert the release is serving.
why_hollow: Both smoke phases execute inside the `app` container and only exercise the HTTP read surface (GET /health, GET /creators/me, GET /videos; dna/insights/billing_balance and the single write probe are required=False, WARN-only). /health aggregates _check_postgres, _check_redis and _check_storage — there is no Celery ping, no queue-depth read, no worker heartbeat. The rollout step has no --wait, so it does not block on container health either. Therefore worker, render-worker and beat can all be crash-looping (bad env, import error, missing native dep) while `up -d` exits 0, /health returns status "ok", llm_harness prints "ALL REQUIRED STEPS PASSED", the deploy job reports success, and the autoheal sidecar (docker-compose.prod.yml:144-146) silently restarts them forever — with 100% of the product (ingest, transcribe, generate, render, publish) dead. The correct check is already written as compose healthchecks; nothing in the pipeline or the monitor ever reads them. This is the layer beneath the 9-day silent outage (OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:104).
repro: grep -n 'worker\|celery' .github/workflows/deploy.yml  ==> no hits inside the smoke step; grep -n 'celery\|queue\|worker' main.py ==> no hits in the /health handler. Live: `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml stop worker render-worker beat` then `curl localhost:8000/health` ==> {"status":"ok",...} and `python3 scripts/llm_harness.py --flow core` ==> ALL REQUIRED STEPS PASSED.
modality: D — Log, counter and status honesty

title: clips_ready notification fires unconditionally on zero clips — "Your 0 clips ... are ready for review."
evidence: worker/tasks.py:3870-3885 (gate is only `if clip_creator_id is not None:`; send_notification.delay(..., "clips_ready", ...) at :3872-3874, clip_count=len(clips)); notify/templates/clips_ready.txt; worker/tasks.py:6896-6900 (in-app copy); clip_engine/ranking.py:408-409 (`if not ranked: return []`, silent, no count); tests/test_notifications_triggers.py:57-110
claims_to_verify: The email subject "Your clips are ready to review", the body "Your {{clip_count}} clip{{s}} ... are ready for review", and the in-app notification "We found candidate clips from your video" all assert that clips exist. A NotificationDelivery row with status=sent is written for it.
why_hollow: The enqueue is gated only on the creator existing, never on len(clips). Zero clips is a first-class reachable state: persist_ranked_clips returns [] on `if not ranked` (a silent boundary with no log and no count) whenever score_and_rank produces nothing — flat-energy source, empty transcript, no retention curve, or (per D-7b) a wholly-empty LLM score set. The terminal SSE event one line earlier is already honest (message=f"Generated {len(clips)} clip(s).") — the email is not. No test covers the zero case: the only trigger test fixes two mock clips and its docstring reads "after a successful clip generation", baking the assumption in.

title: Deploy "Preflight check" never runs a single external-API probe — doctor.py is invoked without --full
claims_to_verify: A GitHub Actions step named "Preflight check", sited between docker pull and alembic upgrade head, that gates every production deploy. docs/SECRETS.md, docs/ACCESS.md:278 and LEFT_OFF.md:114 treat it as the credential-verification ritual, and the Phase-1 pack (d08-deploy-observability.md:153) states as fact that it 'live-probes Postgres, Redis, Anthropic, Voyage, Deepgram, R2 and Stripe'.
why_hollow: scripts/doctor.py:461 gates _live_anthropic/_live_voyage/_live_deepgram/_live_r2/_live_stripe behind `if full:`. Both deploy paths run bare `python scripts/doctor.py`, so only string/format checks plus SELECT 1 and PING run. `--full` appears in zero workflows and zero scripts — the only two code hits are doctor.py's own docstring (:16) and its own argparse declaration (:500); every other hit is prose in eight docs. The consequence is that the 2026-08-13 fix that rewrote _live_stripe to probe through billing.stripe_client._STRIPE — written expressly to stop the 10-week outage recurring (OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:148) — has never executed on a deploy, and neither has the matching _live_r2 fix. Secondary: has_failures() (doctor.py:477) counts only Status.FAIL, and every _live_* probe returns Status.SKIP when its key is absent, so SKIP can never fail the gate.
repro: git grep -n -- "--full" .github/ scripts/ | grep -i doctor   # only doctor.py's own docstring + argparse. Then, showing PASS/exit 0 with every external credential bogus: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$HOME ENV=production DATABASE_URL='postgresql://u:p@h:5432/d' REDIS_URL='redis://h:6379/0' ALLOWED_ORIGINS='https://autoclip.studio' POSTGRES_PASSWORD=x TRANSCRIPTION_BACKEND=deepgram JWT_SECRET_KEY="$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '\n')" TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(.venv/bin/python -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet;print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())')" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-COMPLETELY-BOGUS' VOYAGE_API_KEY='pa-BOGUS' DEEPGRAM_API_KEY='0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567' STORAGE_BACKEND=r2 R2_ACCOUNT_ID=bogus R2_BUCKET=bogus R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID=bogus R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=bogus STRIPE_SECRET_KEY='sk_live_TOTALLY_BOGUS' STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET='whsec_bogus' STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY='pk_live_bogus' GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID='x.apps.googleusercontent.com' GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET='y' OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI='https://autoclip.studio/this/route/does/not/exist' CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN='tok' .venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py --offline; echo EXIT=$?   ->  '23 ok · 0 warn · 0 fail · 0 skipped / Result: PASS / EXIT=0'

title: Staging-parity gate has no render-queue consumer and a different storage backend; the test named test_staging_prod_compose_parity checks neither
claims_to_verify: deploy.yml:31-147 'Staging gate (data-bearing DB)', a hard `needs:` dependency of the prod deploy job and described in the ground-truth process map as 'the strongest gate in the pipeline'. tests/test_ci_config.py:298 exists specifically so that 'a version skew would [not] make the gate's green meaningless'.
why_hollow: worker/celery_app.py:84 routes render_clip, render_video_clips, clean_clip, edit_clip and render_summary to the dedicated `render` queue. Prod runs two workers (prod:46 `-Q celery`, prod:72 `-Q render`); staging runs ONE worker with no -Q at all (staging:131), so it consumes only the default queue and every render task enqueued on ccstage sits unconsumed forever while the API answers 202. Staging also pins STORAGE_BACKEND: local (staging:89,126) where prod pins r2 authoritatively (deploy.yml:250-256) — and routers/videos.py:288-293 409s the whole browser->R2 presigned multipart upload path when the backend is not r2, so Issue 395's upload path cannot run in staging by construction. Staging has no `beat` service, so nothing scheduled is exercised either. The parity test asserts exactly four things: the postgres image string, the redis image string, that staging's app/worker image is ${STAGING_IMAGE:-creatorclip:staging}, and that pgbouncer is absent from prod — nothing about the service set, queue topology, STORAGE_BACKEND, or command:. The gate's smoke is llm_harness --flow core (health, auth_me, videos_list, dna, insights, billing_balance, envelope shape) — no render, no upload.
repro: .venv/bin/python -c "import yaml; p=yaml.safe_load(open('docker-compose.prod.yml'))['services']; s=yaml.safe_load(open('docker-compose.staging.yml'))['services']; print(sorted(p)); print(sorted(s)); print(p['worker']['command']); print(p['render-worker']['command']); print(s['worker']['command']); print(s['app']['environment']['STORAGE_BACKEND']); from worker.celery_app import RENDER_QUEUE, RENDER_TASKS; print(RENDER_QUEUE, list(RENDER_TASKS))"  then  pytest tests/test_ci_config.py::test_staging_prod_compose_parity -q  -> passes
modality: E — Config, flags, and external registration

title: Every transactional email is recorded status=sent over a console sink, and the lifecycle sweep short-circuits into a green Celery success
evidence: worker/tasks.py:6730-6738 (row written sent before dispatch), worker/tasks.py:4556-4561 (silent-skip), notify/mailer.py:183-189 (_send_console), config.py:993 NOTIFY_BACKEND="console", config.py:1010 MAILING_ADDRESS="", worker/schedule.py:77
claims_to_verify: The notification_deliveries table is the app's own record that an email was delivered, and doubles as the idempotency latch. run_lifecycle_scan is a beat-scheduled Celery task whose completion is counted as CELERY_TASKS_TOTAL{status=success}.
why_hollow: worker/tasks.py:6730-6738 inserts the delivery row with status=NotificationDeliveryStatus.sent BEFORE the mailer is called (the send is deliberately deferred until after the session closes). With NOTIFY_BACKEND="console" — the config default — notify/mailer.py:183 dispatches to _send_console, which is a logger.info and by its own docstring 'never calls any external service'. No exception is raised so the row is never downgraded to failed, and the UNIQUE dedupe_key short-circuit at worker/tasks.py:6741-6759 only retries rows whose status is `failed` — so a later switch to NOTIFY_BACKEND=resend can never re-send any of them. Separately, worker/tasks.py:4556 is `if not settings.MAILING_ADDRESS: logger.info(...); return`, no-opping the entire welcome/nudge/re-engagement sweep at INFO level while the task reports SUCCESS. Neither NOTIFY_BACKEND nor MAILING_ADDRESS appears in any deployment artifact (grep over .github/workflows/, docker-compose*.yml and deploy/ returns nothing; only render.yaml:27, the unused path); config.py:1130 _require_prod_secrets checks neither; scripts/doctor.py has no notifications section; /health does not report the backend. The production value is unknowable from the repo and the failure mode is total silence plus a `sent` row.
repro: .venv/bin/python -c "import inspect, notify.mailer as m, worker.tasks as t; from config import settings; print(settings.NOTIFY_BACKEND, repr(settings.MAILING_ADDRESS)); s=inspect.getsource(t.send_notification); print('sent-row precedes send:', s.index('status=NotificationDeliveryStatus.sent') < s.index('mailer.send')); print(inspect.getsource(m._send_console))"  and  grep -rn 'NOTIFY_BACKEND\|MAILING_ADDRESS' .github/workflows/ docker-compose*.yml deploy/   (no hits).  tests/test_lifecycle_email.py:133 is green and its docstring is 'with MAILING_ADDRESS unset the whole sweep is a no-op'.
modality: E — Config, flags, and external registration

title: Two "price-book math" tests assert a*b == a*b over a cost path that does not exist; Deepgram/Voyage/R2/render cost is recorded nowhere
claims_to_verify: tests/test_usage_ledger.py:91 heads the block 'Unit: extended price-book math (Issue 289)'; test_estimate_cost_deepgram_minutes and test_estimate_cost_mixed_llm_and_deepgram read as cost-accounting coverage for the non-LLM half of the ledger. config.py:199 documents PRICE_BOOK_VERSION as 'a version mismatch between a stored cost_estimate and this stamp signals a rate-change event'.
why_hollow: Neither test calls any production function for the Deepgram part — the test body IS the arithmetic: `expected_usd = minutes * settings.COST_PER_MIN_DEEPGRAM; assert abs(expected_usd - 0.582) < 1e-9` is 60*0.0097 == 0.582, a tautology over two constants; the 'mixed' test hand-rolls the sum the same way at :128. There is no production code that multiplies minutes by COST_PER_MIN_DEEPGRAM: `git grep -n COST_PER_MIN_DEEPGRAM -- '*.py'` hits only config.py:179 and tests/test_usage_ledger.py, and `git grep -n 'deepgram|transcription' billing/` returns nothing. The sweep also found COST_PER_MTOK_VOYAGE, COST_PER_GB_MO_R2, COST_PER_M_R2_CLASS_A, COST_PER_M_R2_CLASS_B, COST_PER_RENDER_CPU_S and RECAP_TARGET_DURATION_MIN_S referenced NOWHERE outside config.py/.env.example/docs, and PRICE_BOOK_VERSION referenced only in tests. So usage_ledger and billing/spend_guard.py account for Anthropic tokens only; transcription minutes (plausibly the largest non-LLM per-job cost), embeddings, storage and render CPU are invisible to the spend guard while a green 'price-book' test block and a rate-change sentinel report otherwise.

title: GDPR data export: three endpoints, a table, a Celery task, and a published Privacy Policy promise, with zero UI
claims_to_verify: routers/export.py:1 declares 'GDPR Art. 15/20 data export (Issue 249)'. static/privacy.html:162, live in production, promises creators: 'you may request a copy of your data at any time ... The export is prepared on request and made available as a download from your account.'
why_hollow: There is no affordance anywhere in the React app to request or download an export — not on Profile, not on Settings, not in any component. The sibling right-to-erasure capability (DELETE /auth/me) DID get a UI (Profile 'Danger zone', Issue 158, ticked in CLAUDE.md's pre-launch list), so this is an omission and not a house convention. The only way a creator can exercise Art. 20 portability is to hand-craft an authenticated POST. The response-field diff independently flagged ExportStatusOut.requested_at and ExportStatusOut.completed_at as reaching no client — what a response model with no client looks like from the other side.

title: The `usage` cost ledger is written on every billed LLM call and read by nothing; two of its columns are never even written
evidence: models.py:1304 (Usage), billing/ledger.py:75 (increment_usage), billing/ledger.py:248-254 (record_llm_usage tail), models.py:1312-1313 (videos_processed, clips_generated), tests/test_usage_coverage.py:1-16
claims_to_verify: tests/test_usage_coverage.py:1-16 — a repo-wide AST gate — states that record_llm_usage 'is the billing ledger write that deducts from the creator's token/minute pack. If a task runs inference without calling it, creators get LLM calls that are unmetered — a real revenue leak at scale.' models.py:1316-1319 adds that cost_estimate is 'persisted at write time so billing/metrics can read USD without a price-book join at query time.'
why_hollow: record_llm_usage never touches Creator.minutes_balance or MinuteDeduction — minutes are deducted from video duration at ingest (worker/tasks.py:2212), a separate path. No creator has ever been charged from `usage`. The table has zero readers: no select(Usage), no /usage endpoint, no raw SQL, no reconciliation job. billing/spend_guard.py — the thing that does consume cost — reads Redis µ$ counters and imports only Creator from models (spend_guard.py:56). The other two consumers at ledger.py:236-246 are the Prometheus counter (dead, see F3) and Redis. Usage.videos_processed and Usage.clips_generated are never written either — declared, migrated, permanently 0. Cost: every billed LLM call opens a second admin DB session and runs an ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE inside a savepoint on the hot path of ~41 Celery tasks to write a row nobody reads. docs/GO_LIVE.md:83 asks 'Will we hear about cost blowouts?' and answers OPEN — the durable ledger that would answer it exists and is unread.
repro: grep -rn "select(Usage|FROM usage|Usage\." --include="*.py" routers worker billing scripts *.py | grep -v billing/ledger.py   → 0 hits (no reader anywhere);  grep -rnw "videos_processed|clips_generated" --include="*.py" . | grep -v models.py   → 0 hits

title: Six of twelve Prometheus metrics are incremented in a different container from the only /metrics exporter — METRICS_TOKEN is irrelevant; plus a daily paid R2 bucket sweep that feeds two of them
evidence: observability.py:33 (single default registry), observability.py:582 + main.py:476-498 (the only exporter, app process), worker/tasks.py:228/954/1406-1407, observability.py:603-606, worker/tasks.py:1385 (collect_storage_gauges), worker/schedule.py:107, worker/storage.py:117-133, docker-compose.prod.yml:2/35/56/82
claims_to_verify: The 12 metrics are described as instrumented business observability; the Phase-1 finding and process-map.md:298-302 attribute their absence to a single cause — '/metrics auto-disables in production if METRICS_TOKEN is unset' — which implies setting METRICS_TOKEN would restore them. worker/tasks.py:1385 claims a 'daily storage-footprint sweep for object-storage COGS' (Issue 293).
why_hollow: prometheus_client keeps counters in a PER-PROCESS registry. generate_latest() is called only from the FastAPI /metrics route in the `app` container. There is no PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR, no start_http_server, no make_asgi_app, no pushgateway anywhere in the tree, and prod runs four separate containers (app, worker, render-worker, beat). So BEAT_LOCK_SKIPS_TOTAL, RENDER_FAILURES_TOTAL, R2_BYTES_STORED, R2_OBJECTS, CELERY_TASK_DURATION and CELERY_TASKS_TOTAL can NEVER be scraped, and LLM_TOKENS_TOTAL / LLM_COST_USD_TOTAL expose only the small app-side sliver (most LLM calls — DNA build, clip scoring, video context, chapters, hooks, titles, improvement brief, thumbnail concepts — run in Celery). Rider: collect_storage_gauges paginates the ENTIRE R2 bucket across five prefixes daily (list_objects_v2, billable, unbounded in object count) for the sole purpose of calling .set() on two gauges in the beat process; the result is discarded on process exit, never logged, never persisted, never compared to a threshold. This corrects rather than repeats the Phase-1 metrics finding: fixing METRICS_TOKEN will not restore any of these.
repro: grep -rn "start_http_server|make_asgi_app|PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC|multiproc" --include="*.py" .   → 0 hits;  grep -rn "generate_latest" --include="*.py" .   → exactly 2 (import + observability.py:582);  grep -n "^  [a-z]" docker-compose.prod.yml   → app/worker/render-worker/beat. Live: set METRICS_TOKEN, curl /metrics, observe celery_tasks_total, render_failures_total, beat_lock_skips_total, r2_bytes_stored, r2_objects absent no matter how much work the workers do.
modality: F — Dead output: built, emitted, and consumed by nothing
